# Parse the archive file content to extract song titles and artists
import re

content = file_data['content']
lines = content.strip().split('\n')
songs_to_archive = []
for line in lines:
    line = line.strip()
    if line.startswith('- '):
        # Format: "- Title by Artist"
        # Remove the leading "- "
        song_str = line[2:]
        # Split on " by " (case sensitive? We'll use regex)
        match = re.match(r'^(.*?)\s+by\s+(.*)$', song_str)
        if match:
            title = match.group(1).strip()
            artist = match.group(2).strip()
            songs_to_archive.append({'title': title, 'artist': artist})
        else:
            # If no "by", treat whole as title
            songs_to_archive.append({'title': song_str, 'artist': None})

print(songs_to_archive)

playlists = []
page_index = 0
while True:
    result = apis.spotify.show_playlist_library(access_token=spotify_login['access_token'], page_index=page_index, page_limit=20)
    if not result:
        break
    playlists.extend(result)
    if len(result) < 20:
        break
    page_index += 1

# Let's parse the archive file content to extract song titles and artists.
import re

content = file_data['content']
lines = content.strip().split('\n')
archive_songs = []
for line in lines:
    line = line.strip()
    if line.startswith('- '):
        song_str = line[2:]
        # Format: "Title by Artist"
        if ' by ' in song_str:
            title, artist = song_str.rsplit(' by ', 1)
            archive_songs.append((title.strip(), artist.strip()))
        else:
            # If no "by", just treat as title
            archive_songs.append((song_str.strip(), None))

print(f"Parsed {len(archive_songs)} songs from archive file:")
for t, a in archive_songs:
    print(f"  {t} by {a}")

# Now we have all song_ids. Let's create a set of archive song_ids for quick lookup.
archive_song_ids = {song_id for song_id, _, _ in song_ids_to_archive}
print(f"Archive song IDs: {archive_song_ids}")

# We'll collect all song_ids that are actually removed from any playlist
removed_song_ids = set()

# Iterate over each playlist (excluding the new "Old Songs" playlist 654)
for playlist in all_playlists:
    playlist_id = playlist["playlist_id"]
    song_ids_in_playlist = playlist["song_ids"]
    # Find which songs in this playlist are in the archive set
    to_remove = [sid for sid in song_ids_in_playlist if sid in archive_song_ids]
    if to_remove:
        print(f"Playlist {playlist_id} ({playlist['title']}) has {len(to_remove)} songs to remove: {to_remove}")
        for sid in to_remove:
            # Remove from this playlist
            result = apis.spotify.remove_song_from_playlist(playlist_id=playlist_id, song_id=sid, access_token=login_result["access_token"])
            print(f"  Removed song {sid} from playlist {playlist_id}: {result}")
            removed_song_ids.add(sid)
    else:
        print(f"Playlist {playlist_id} ({playlist['title']}) has no archive songs.")

print(f"\nTotal unique songs removed: {len(removed_song_ids)}")
print(f"Removed song IDs: {removed_song_ids}")

# Now add all removed songs to the "Old Songs" playlist (id 654)

for song_id, title, artist in song_ids_to_archive:
    result = apis.spotify.add_song_to_playlist(playlist_id=old_playlist_id, song_id=song_id, access_token=login_result["access_token"])

# Verify the "Old Songs" playlist now contains all 18 songs

- When Dawn Breaks Without You by Lucas Grey
- Secrets of the Heart by Carter Knight

    line = line.strip()
    if not line:

        old_songs.append((title.strip(), set(artists)))
    else:

steps.code:
# Parse the note content to extract song info
import re

content = note['content']
lines = content.strip().split('\n')
songs = []
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith('- '):
        line = line[2:]
        # Split on " BY " and " RELEASED_AT "
        parts = re.split(r'\s+BY\s+|\s+RELEASED_AT\s+', line)
        if len(parts) == 3:
            title = parts[0].strip()
            artists_str = parts[1].strip()
            release = parts[2].strip()
            artists = [a.strip() for a in artists_str.split(',')]
            songs.append({'title': title, 'artists': artists, 'release': release})
        else:
            print("Could not parse line:", line)

print("Parsed songs count:", len(songs))
for s in songs:
    print(s)

# We need to get release dates for the 10 songs from earlier. Let's re-query them to get their release dates.
# Define the queries for the 10 songs we need release dates for.
queries = [
    ('Tangled Lies', 'TangledLiesAvaMorgan'),
    ('Lost in the Wilderness of Love', 'LostintheWildernessofLoveLilyMoonZoeyJames'),
    ('Whispers of a Forgotten Love', 'WhispersofaForgottenLoveLilyMoonZoeyJames'),
    ('Lost in the Twilight of Hope', 'LostintheTwilightofHopeFelixBlackwood'),
    ('The Distance Between Two Hearts', 'TheDistanceBetweenTwoHeartsJasperSkye'),
    ('When All Hope Seems Lost', 'WhenAllHopeSeemsLostSeraphinaDawn'),
    ('The Forgotten Pages of Time', 'TheForgottenPagesofTimeLunaStarlight'),
    ("Summer's End", "Summer'sEndEthanWallace"),
    ('A Tale of Unspoken Longing', 'ATaleofUnspokenLongingEmilyRivers'),
    ('Cracks in the Facade of Love', 'CracksintheFacadeofLoveVelvetEcho'),
]

release_months = {}

for title, query in queries:
    result = apis.spotify.search_songs(query=query, page_limit=5)
    # Find the first result that matches the title exactly
    for song in result:
        if song['title'].lower() == title.lower():
            release_date = song['release_date']  # e.g., "2020-07-04T18:13:52"
            # Extract month and year
            month = release_date[5:7]  # MM
            year = release_date[0:4]    # YYYY
            release_months[title] = f"{month}/{year}"
            break
    else:
        print(f"Could not find {title} in search results")

print(release_months)

release_months = {
    "Tangled Lies": "12/2022",
    "Lost in the Wilderness of Love": "02/2022",
    "Whispers of a Forgotten Love": "02/2022",
    "Lost in the Twilight of Hope": "07/2022",

    "Mystic Voyage to Avalon": "08/2020",
}

content = note['content']

lines = content.split('\n')

# Process each line
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title: line format is "- <title> BY <artists> RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Find the part after "- " and before " BY "
        # We'll use split
        # Example: "- Tangled Lies BY Ava Morgan RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # After removing leading "- ", we get "Tangled Lies BY Ava Morgan RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Then split on " BY " to get title
        title_part = line.split(' BY ')[0].lstrip('- ').strip()
        # Get the month
        month = release_months.get(title_part)
        if month:
            # Replace TODO with month
            line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', f'RELEASED_AT {month}')
        else:
            print(f"Warning: No month found for {title_part}")
    new_lines.append(line)

new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)

# Print the new content to verify
print(new_content)

            artists_str = m.group(2)
            released = m.group(3)

# Now we have all release dates. Let's build the mapping and update the note.
release_dates = {
    "Lost in the Embrace of Night": "03/2021",
    "Lonely Skies": "11/2022",
    "Caught in a Web of Lies": "03/2021",
    "On the Border of Reality": "08/2022",
    "A Love That Never Was": "10/2020",
    "Astral Serenity": "12/2019",
    "Between Reality and Reverie": "03/2020",
    "Strangers Again": "06/2022",
    "The Mirage of a Perfect Life": "11/2020",
    "Wilted Roses on the Vine": "02/2020",
    "When All Words Fail Us": "07/2020",
    "Final Echo": "07/2022"
}

# Build new content by replacing TODO with the correct date
lines = note["content"].split("\n")
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if "RELEASED_AT TODO" in line:
        # Extract song title: line format "- <title> BY <artists> RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Find the title between "- " and " BY "
        title = line.split(" BY ")[0].lstrip("- ").strip()
        if title in release_dates:
            line = line.replace("RELEASED_AT TODO", "RELEASED_AT " + release_dates[title])
        else:
            print("Warning: no date for", title)
    new_lines.append(line)

new_content = "\n".join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# Build the new content by replacing each TODO with the correct release month/year
import re

# Mapping of song title to release month/year (MM/YYYY)
release_map = {
    "Lost in the Embrace of Night": "03/2021",
    "Lonely Skies": "11/2022",
    "Caught in a Web of Lies": "03/2021",
    "On the Border of Reality": "08/2022",
    "A Love That Never Was": "10/2020",
    "Astral Serenity": "12/2019",
    "Between Reality and Reverie": "03/2020",
    "Strangers Again": "06/2022",
    "The Mirage of a Perfect Life": "11/2020",
    "Wilted Roses on the Vine": "02/2020",
    "When All Words Fail Us": "07/2020",
    "Final Echo": "07/2022"
}

content = note["content"]
lines = content.split("\n")
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if "RELEASED_AT TODO" in line:
        # Extract song title: after "- " and before " BY "
        # Format: "- Song Title BY Artist(s) RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # We'll find the part between "- " and " BY "
        match = re.match(r"^- (.+?) BY .+ RELEASED_AT TODO$", line)
        if match:
            song_title = match.group(1)
            if song_title in release_map:
                new_line = line.replace("RELEASED_AT TODO", "RELEASED_AT " + release_map[song_title])
                new_lines.append(new_line)
            else:
                # Should not happen, but keep as is
                new_lines.append(line)
        else:
            new_lines.append(line)
    else:
        new_lines.append(line)

new_content = "\n".join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# Create mapping of song titles to release month/year
release_dates = {
    "Lost in the Embrace of Night": "03/2021",
    "Lonely Skies": "11/2022",
    "Caught in a Web of Lies": "03/2021",
    "On the Border of Reality": "08/2022",
    "A Love That Never Was": "10/2020",
    "Astral Serenity": "12/2019",
    "Between Reality and Reverie": "03/2020",
    "Strangers Again": "06/2022",
    "The Mirage of a Perfect Life": "11/2020",
    "Wilted Roses on the Vine": "02/2020",
    "When All Words Fail Us": "07/2020",
    "Final Echo": "07/2022"
}

# Update the note content by replacing TODO with the release month/year
new_content = note['content']
for song, date in release_dates.items():
    new_content = new_content.replace(f"{song} BY", f"{song} BY")  # no change needed
    # Replace the TODO after the song line
    # We'll replace "RELEASED_AT TODO" with "RELEASED_AT {date}" for each song
    # But we need to be careful: the line contains the song title and artist, then RELEASED_AT TODO
    # We'll replace the specific pattern: song title + " RELEASED_AT TODO" -> song title + " RELEASED_AT " + date
    # But the line has "BY ... RELEASED_AT TODO", so we can replace "RELEASED_AT TODO" globally, but that would replace all TODO with the same date.
    # So we need to replace per line. We'll split lines and process.
    pass

# Better approach: split lines and replace TODO with the correct date based on song title
lines = new_content.split('\n')
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Find the song title in the line
        # The line format: "- Song Title BY Artist1, Artist2 RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Extract song title: after "- " and before " BY"
        song_title = line.split(' BY ')[0].lstrip('- ').strip()
        if song_title in release_dates:
            line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', f'RELEASED_AT {release_dates[song_title]}')
    new_lines.append(line)
new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# Build mapping of song title to release month/year
release_map = {
    "Lost in the Embrace of Night": "03/2021",
    "Lonely Skies": "11/2022",
    "Caught in a Web of Lies": "03/2021",
    "On the Border of Reality": "08/2022",
    "A Love That Never Was": "10/2020",
    "Astral Serenity": "12/2019",
    "Between Reality and Reverie": "03/2020",
    "Strangers Again": "06/2022",
    "The Mirage of a Perfect Life": "11/2020",
    "Wilted Roses on the Vine": "02/2020",
    "When All Words Fail Us": "07/2020",
    "Final Echo": "07/2022"
}

# Get the current content
content = note["content"]

# Split into lines and replace TODO for each song
lines = content.split("\n")
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if "RELEASED_AT TODO" in line:
        # Extract song title: line format "- <title> BY <artists> RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Find the part before " BY "
        title_part = line.split(" BY ")[0].lstrip("- ").strip()
        # Get the release month/year
        release = release_map.get(title_part)
        if release:
            line = line.replace("RELEASED_AT TODO", f"RELEASED_AT {release}")
        else:
            print(f"Warning: no release found for {title_part}")
    new_lines.append(line)

new_content = "\n".join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# Build mapping from song title to release month/year
release_map = {
    "Lost in the Embrace of Night": "03/2021",
    "Lonely Skies": "11/2022",
    "Caught in a Web of Lies": "03/2021",
    "On the Border of Reality": "08/2022",
    "A Love That Never Was": "10/2020",
    "Astral Serenity": "12/2019",
    "Between Reality and Reverie": "03/2020",
    "Strangers Again": "06/2022",
    "The Mirage of a Perfect Life": "11/2020",
    "Wilted Roses on the Vine": "02/2020",
    "When All Words Fail Us": "07/2020",
    "Final Echo": "07/2022"
}

# Update the note content
lines = note["content"].split("\n")
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if "RELEASED_AT TODO" in line:
        # Extract song title: line starts with "- " and has " BY " before artists
        # e.g., "- Lost in the Embrace of Night BY Noah Bennett RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Split on " BY " to get title part
        title_part = line.split(" BY ")[0].lstrip("- ").strip()
        if title_part in release_map:
            line = line.replace("RELEASED_AT TODO", "RELEASED_AT " + release_map[title_part])
        else:
            print("Warning: no release date for", title_part)
    new_lines.append(line)
new_content = "\n".join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# Let's check the update_note API specification to know the exact parameters.
print(apis.api_docs.show_api_doc(app_name='simple_note', api_name='update_note'))

# Now we have all release dates. Let's build the updated content by replacing each TODO with the correct month/year.
# Mapping song title -> release month/year (MM/YYYY)
release_map = {
    "Silver Lining": "12/2022",
    "Walking Through the Valley of Shadows": "08/2022",
    "Where Shadows Come to Life": "01/2023",
    "Eternal Melancholy": "04/2023",
    "Crimson Veil": "01/2020",
    "Elusive Joy": "03/2021",
    "Ephemeral Beauty": "01/2020",
    "Stardust Serenade": "04/2019",
    "Veiled Behind a Mask of Joy": "10/2022",
    "In the Wake of Unspoken Promises": "07/2022",
    "Wading Through the Ashes of Love": "09/2020",
    "Fading Like a Distant Star": "01/2019",
    "Wilted Grace": "01/2022",
}

# Get current note content
note = apis.simple_note.show_note(access_token=access_token, note_id=3084)
content = note["content"]

# Replace each TODO with the correct date based on song title
for title, date in release_map.items():
    # Find the line containing this title and replace "TODO" with date
    # We'll do a simple string replacement on the whole content, but ensure we only replace the TODO after that title.
    # Since each line is unique, we can replace "RELEASED_AT TODO" with "RELEASED_AT {date}" for lines containing the title.
    # We'll split lines and rebuild.
    lines = content.split("\n")
    new_lines = []
    for line in lines:
        if title in line and "RELEASED_AT TODO" in line:
            line = line.replace("RELEASED_AT TODO", f"RELEASED_AT {date}")
        new_lines.append(line)
    content = "\n".join(new_lines)

# Print the new content to verify
print(content)

# Now let's update the note content with the release months for all TODO songs.
# We'll replace each TODO line with the correct release month.

current_content = """# Spotify Liked Songs
- When Angels Weep for Us BY Lucas Grey, Velvet Echo RELEASED_AT 07/2022
- Unspoken Words BY Aria Sterling RELEASED_AT 06/2021
- Time's Hold BY Aria Sterling RELEASED_AT 11/2022
- Bleeding Sun BY Aria Sterling RELEASED_AT 11/2022
- Distant Love BY Ava Morgan RELEASED_AT 12/2022
- Silver Lining BY Ava Morgan RELEASED_AT TODO
- Walking Through the Valley of Shadows BY Lily Moon, Zoey James RELEASED_AT TODO
- Where Shadows Come to Life BY Olivia Roberts RELEASED_AT TODO
- Eternal Melancholy BY Olivia Roberts RELEASED_AT TODO
- Crimson Veil BY Phoenix Rivers RELEASED_AT TODO
- Elusive Joy BY Orion Steele RELEASED_AT TODO
- Ephemeral Beauty BY Eliana Harper RELEASED_AT TODO
- Stardust Serenade BY Violet Cascade RELEASED_AT TODO
- Veiled Behind a Mask of Joy BY Liam Palmer RELEASED_AT TODO
- In the Wake of Unspoken Promises BY Isabella Cruz RELEASED_AT TODO
- Wading Through the Ashes of Love BY Marcus Lane RELEASED_AT TODO
- Fading Like a Distant Star BY Hazel Winter RELEASED_AT TODO
- Wilted Grace BY Felix Blackwood RELEASED_AT TODO
"""

# Mapping of song title to release month (MM/YYYY)
release_months = {
    "Silver Lining": "12/2022",
    "Walking Through the Valley of Shadows": "08/2022",
    "Where Shadows Come to Life": "01/2023",
    "Eternal Melancholy": "04/2023",
    "Crimson Veil": "01/2020",
    "Elusive Joy": "03/2021",
    "Ephemeral Beauty": "01/2020",
    "Stardust Serenade": "04/2019",
    "Veiled Behind a Mask of Joy": "10/2022",
    "In the Wake of Unspoken Promises": "07/2022",
    "Wading Through the Ashes of Love": "09/2020",
    "Fading Like a Distant Star": "01/2019",
    "Wilted Grace": "01/2022"
}

# Build new content by replacing TODO lines
new_lines = []
for line in current_content.split('\n'):
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title: line format "- <title> BY <artists> RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # The title is between "- " and " BY "
        title = line.split(' BY ')[0][2:]
        if title in release_months:
            line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', f'RELEASED_AT {release_months[title]}')
        else:
            print(f"Warning: No release month found for {title}")
    new_lines.append(line)

new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# We have the note content and the release dates. Let's update the note by replacing each "RELEASED_AT TODO" with the corresponding date.
# We'll process each line, find the song title, and replace the TODO with the date from song_release_dates.

new_lines = []
for line in note_content.split('\n'):
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title: the part before " BY "
        # The line format: "- Song Title BY Artist RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # We'll split on " BY " to get the song title (first part after "- ")
        parts = line.split(' BY ')
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            song_title = parts[0].strip().lstrip('- ').strip()
            # Look up the date
            date = song_release_dates.get(song_title)
            if date:
                line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', 'RELEASED_AT ' + date)
            else:
                # If not found, leave as is (shouldn't happen)
                pass
    new_lines.append(line)

new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# Fetch all liked songs (paginated)
liked_songs = []
page_index = 0
page_limit = 20
while True:
    page = apis.spotify.show_liked_songs(access_token=access_token, page_index=page_index, page_limit=page_limit)
    if not page:
        break
    liked_songs.extend(page)
    if len(page) < page_limit:
        break
    page_index += 1

liked_song_ids = {song['song_id'] for song in liked_songs}
print(f"Total liked songs: {len(liked_song_ids)}")
print(f"Liked song IDs: {sorted(liked_song_ids)}")

# Identify unliked songs in the queue and remove them (from highest position to lowest)
unliked_positions = [song['position'] for song in queue if song['song_id'] not in liked_song_ids]
print(f"Unliked positions to remove: {unliked_positions}")

# Remove in descending order to avoid index shifting
for pos in sorted(unliked_positions, reverse=True):
    result = apis.spotify.remove_song_from_queue(position=pos, access_token=access_token)
    print(f"Removed position {pos}: {result}")

# Verify the updated queue contains only liked songs
updated_queue = apis.spotify.show_song_queue(access_token=access_token)
remaining_ids = [song['song_id'] for song in updated_queue]
print(f"Remaining queue song IDs: {remaining_ids}")
print(f"All remaining are liked: {set(remaining_ids).issubset(liked_song_ids)}")
